entries.value: Dust and rubble, long undisturbed
Water drips steadily from the ceiling
Old bones picked clean in a corner
Scorch marks blacken one wall
A cold draft from an unseen gap
Broken furniture and a faded tapestry
Faint scratching echoes from the walls
A foul smell with no obvious source
Claw marks gouged into the stone floor
Guttered candle stubs and a circle of ash
Cobwebs drape every corner, grey and heavy with age
Rusted chains dangle from an iron ring set in the ceiling
Mould spreads across the walls in dark, creeping maps
A shattered clay urn, its contents long since spilled
A dried bloodstain fans across the flagstones
Tally-marks are scratched into one wall, hundreds of them
A toppled column lies cracked across the floor
The cold remains of a cooking fire, ashes grey and scattered
A rusted helm sits alone in the middle of the floor
Roots have broken through the ceiling and hang like hair
The air hangs thick with the smell of damp earth
A crude drawing of a horned figure marks one wall
Black puddles pool in the uneven floor, still as glass
A broken shield leans forgotten against the far wall
Something small skitters away the moment you enter
The flagstones are worn smooth by long-vanished feet
A tattered bedroll rots in one corner
Splintered crates lie stacked and empty
A faded chalk circle rings the centre of the room
Deep gouges score the door, as if something clawed to get out
The ceiling sags, its timbers black with rot
A cold hearth, its chimney choked with debris
Salt-white streaks weep down the walls
An iron manacle, still locked, hangs empty from the wall
Dead leaves have drifted into the corners
The far wall is stained with old smoke, floor to ceiling
A dry, cracked wineskin lies discarded
Pale fungus clusters swollen in the damp corners
A cracked mirror leans against the wall, its silver gone black
Iron sconces line the walls, their torches long since spent
A stone bench, split down the middle, faces nothing
The floor tilts toward a rusted drain grate
